title: After Twenty Years
author: O. Henry
intro: 两个在纽约一起长大的好友约定二十年后原地重逢。今晚，赴约的人等在旧饭馆门口，而巡逻的警察……欧·亨利笔下最著名的反转短篇之一。

paragraphs.en: The policeman on the beat moved up the avenue impressively. The impressiveness was habitual and not for show, for spectators were few. The time was barely 10 o'clock at night, but chilly gusts of wind with a taste of rain in them had well nigh depeopled the streets.
paragraphs.zh: 巡逻的警察威风凛凛地沿大街走来。这种威风是习惯性的，并非做给人看，因为路上行人寥寥。时间才晚上十点，可带着雨意的阵阵寒风几乎已把街上的人吹得不见踪影。

paragraphs.en: Trying doors as he went, twirling his club with many intricate and artful movements, turning now and then to cast his watchful eye adown the pacific thoroughfare, the officer, with his stalwart form and slight swagger, made a fine picture of a guardian of the peace.
paragraphs.zh: 他一边走一边试着推推店门，手里的警棍滴溜溜转着各种花式，不时回头向这条平静的大街投去警觉的一瞥。他身材魁梧，步态微带神气，活脱脱一幅治安守护者的画面。

paragraphs.en: The vicinity was one that kept early hours. Now and then you might see the lights of a cigar store or of an all-night lunch counter; but the majority of the doors belonged to business places that had long since been closed.
paragraphs.zh: 这一带歇业很早。偶尔还能看到一家雪茄店或通宵小吃摊的灯光，但多数店门早已紧闭。

paragraphs.en: When about midway of a certain block the policeman suddenly slowed his walk. In the doorway of a darkened hardware store a man leaned, with an unlighted cigar in his mouth. As the policeman walked up to him the man spoke up quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 走到某条街区的中间时，警察突然放慢了脚步。在一家熄了灯的五金店门口，一个男人倚门而立，嘴里叼着一支没点燃的雪茄。警察走近时，那人先开了口。

paragraphs.en: “It's all right, officer,” he said, reassuringly. “I'm just waiting for a friend. It's an appointment made twenty years ago. Sounds a little funny to you, doesn't it? Well, I'll explain if you'd like to make certain it's all straight. About that long ago there used to be a restaurant where this store stands—'Big Joe' Brady's restaurant.”
paragraphs.zh: 「没事儿，警官，」他宽慰地说，「我在等一位朋友。二十年前约好的。听起来有点可笑吧？要是你想确认我不是在干坏事，我可以解释。大概就是二十年前，现在这家店的位置上原本有家饭馆——『大个子乔』布拉迪饭馆。」

paragraphs.en: “Until five years ago,” said the policeman. “It was torn down then.”
paragraphs.zh: 「五年前还在，」警察说，「那会儿才拆掉的。」

paragraphs.en: The man in the doorway struck a match and lit his cigar. The light showed a pale, square-jawed face with keen eyes, and a little white scar near his right eyebrow. His scarfpin was a large diamond, oddly set.
paragraphs.zh: 门口那人划亮一根火柴点着雪茄。火光映出一张苍白的方下巴脸，目光锐利，右眉梢附近有一道小小的白色疤痕。他的领带别针是一颗大钻石，镶嵌得样式古怪。

paragraphs.en: “Twenty years ago to-night,” said the man, “I dined here at 'Big Joe' Brady's with Jimmy Wells, my best chum, and the finest chap in the world. He and I were raised here in New York, just like two brothers, together. I was eighteen and Jimmy was twenty.”
paragraphs.zh: 「二十年前的今晚，」那人说，「我就在这儿，在『大个子乔』布拉迪饭馆和吉米·威尔斯一起吃饭。他是我最好的伙伴，世上最棒的小伙子。我俩在纽约一起长大，亲如兄弟。我十八岁，吉米二十岁。」

paragraphs.en: “The next morning I was to start for the West to make my fortune. You couldn't have dragged Jimmy out of New York; he thought it was the only place on earth. Well, we agreed that night that we would meet here again exactly twenty years from that date and time, no matter what our conditions might be or from what distance we might have to come.”
paragraphs.zh: 「第二天早上我就要去西部闯天下了。可你怎么也拉不动吉米离开纽约，他觉得那是世上唯一的好地方。于是那晚我们约定：整整二十年后的同一日期、同一时间，就在这里重逢，不管彼此境况如何、要从多远赶来。」

paragraphs.en: “We figured that in twenty years each of us ought to have our destiny worked out and our fortunes made, whatever they were going to be.”
paragraphs.zh: 「我们想着，二十年足够各自把命运闯出个结果、把家业挣下个样子，不管那结果是什么。」

paragraphs.en: “It sounds pretty interesting,” said the policeman. “Rather a long time between meets, though, it seems to me. Haven't you heard from your friend since you left?”
paragraphs.zh: 「听着挺有意思，」警察说，「不过在我看来，这两次见面间隔得可够长的。你离开之后就没收到过你朋友的消息吗？」

paragraphs.en: “Well, yes, for a time we corresponded,” said the other. “But after a year or two we lost track of each other. You see, the West is a pretty big proposition, and I kept hustling around over it pretty lively.”
paragraphs.zh: 「哦，有过，头一阵我们还通信，」那人说，「可一两年后就失去了联系。你知道，西部太大了，我又一直在四处奔波忙碌。」

paragraphs.en: “But I know Jimmy will meet me here if he's alive, for he always was the truest, stanchest old chap in the world. He'll never forget. I came a thousand miles to stand in this door to-night, and it's worth it if my old partner turns up.”
paragraphs.zh: 「不过我知道，只要吉米还活着，他一定会来这儿见我，因为他一向是世上最忠诚、最靠得住的老伙计。他绝不会忘。我跑了一千英里，今晚就为站在这扇门口——只要老搭档露面，就值了。」

paragraphs.en: The waiting man pulled out a handsome watch, the lids of it set with small diamonds.
paragraphs.zh: 等候的人掏出一块漂亮的怀表，表盖上镶着小粒钻石。

paragraphs.en: “Three minutes to ten,” he announced. “It was exactly ten o'clock when we parted here at the restaurant door.”
paragraphs.zh: 「差三分十点，」他说，「当年我们就是在饭馆门口分手的，正好十点整。」

paragraphs.en: “Did pretty well out West, didn't you?” asked the policeman.
paragraphs.zh: 「在西部混得不错吧？」警察问。

paragraphs.en: “You bet! I hope Jimmy has done half as well. He was a kind of plodder, though, good fellow as he was. I've had to compete with some of the sharpest wits going to get my pile. A man gets in a groove in New York. It takes the West to put a razor-edge on him.”
paragraphs.zh: 「那当然！但愿吉米也有我一半的成就。不过话说回来，他人虽好，却有点死心眼。我可是跟一帮最精明的脑袋较量过才挣下这份家当的。人在纽约容易困在老套里，只有西部才能把人磨得锋利。」

paragraphs.en: The policeman twirled his club and took a step or two.
paragraphs.zh: 警察转了转警棍，迈开了一两步。

paragraphs.en: “I'll be on my way. Hope your friend comes around all right. Going to call time on him sharp?”
paragraphs.zh: 「我得走了。希望你朋友会来。你会准点等他到时间吗？」

paragraphs.en: “I should say not!” said the other. “I'll give him half an hour at least. If Jimmy is alive on earth he'll be here by that time. So long, officer.”
paragraphs.zh: 「当然不会！」那人说，「我至少等他半小时。只要吉米还活着，到时候一定会来。再见，警官。」

paragraphs.en: “Good-night, sir,” said the policeman, passing on along his beat, trying doors as he went.
paragraphs.zh: 「晚安，先生，」警察说着继续沿巡逻路线走去，边走边推推店门。

paragraphs.en: There was now a fine, cold drizzle falling, and the wind had risen from its uncertain puffs into a steady blow. The few foot passengers astir in that quarter hurried dismally and silently along with coat collars turned high and pocketed hands.
paragraphs.zh: 这时下起了细密的冷雨，风也从一阵阵的乱吹变成了持续不断的劲风。这一带仅有的几个行人把衣领竖得高高的、双手插在口袋里，一言不发地匆匆走过。

paragraphs.en: And in the door of the hardware store the man who had come a thousand miles to fill an appointment, uncertain almost to absurdity, with the friend of his youth, smoked his cigar and waited.
paragraphs.zh: 而五金店门口，那个跑了一千英里来赴一场几乎荒唐可笑的旧约的人，抽着雪茄，等着。

paragraphs.en: About twenty minutes he waited, and then a tall man in a long overcoat, with collar turned up to his ears, hurried across from the opposite side of the street. He went directly to the waiting man.
paragraphs.zh: 他大约等了二十分钟，随后一个身穿长外套、衣领竖到耳根的高个子男人从街对面匆匆走来，径直走向等候的人。

paragraphs.en: “Is that you, Bob?” he asked, doubtfully.
paragraphs.zh: 「是你吗，鲍勃？」他迟疑地问。

paragraphs.en: “Is that you, Jimmy Wells?” cried the man in the door.
paragraphs.zh: 「是你吗，吉米·威尔斯？」门口那人高声说。

paragraphs.en: “Bless my heart!” exclaimed the new arrival, grasping both the other's hands with his own. “It's Bob, sure as fate. I was certain I'd find you here if you were still in existence. Well, well, well!—twenty years is a long time. The old restaurant's gone, Bob; I wish it had lasted, so we could have had another dinner there. How has the West treated you, old man?”
paragraphs.zh: 「天哪！」来人惊呼，双手握住对方的两只手，「果然是鲍勃，一点没错。我就知道你只要还在人世，一定能在这儿找到你。哎呀呀——二十年可真长啊。老饭馆没了，鲍勃；真希望它还在，咱们好再进去吃一顿。西部对你怎么样，老伙计？」

paragraphs.en: “Bully; it has given me everything I asked it for. You've changed lots, Jimmy. I never thought you were so tall by two or three inches.”
paragraphs.zh: 「好极了；我要什么它给什么。你变了很多，吉米。我一直不知道你竟高了我两三英寸。」

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I grew a bit after I was twenty.”
paragraphs.zh: 「哦，我二十岁以后又长了一点个儿。」

paragraphs.en: “Doing well in New York, Jimmy?”
paragraphs.zh: 「在纽约过得不错吧，吉米？」

paragraphs.en: “Moderately. I have a position in one of the city departments. Come on, Bob; we'll go around to a place I know of, and have a good long talk about old times.”
paragraphs.zh: 「还过得去。我在市政部门有个职位。走吧，鲍勃；我知道一个地方，咱们去那儿好好叙叙旧。」

paragraphs.en: The two men started up the street, arm in arm. The man from the West, his egotism enlarged by success, was beginning to outline the history of his career. The other, submerged in his overcoat, listened with interest.
paragraphs.zh: 两人挽着胳膊沿街走去。从西部来的那位因为成功而愈发自负，开始大谈自己的发家史。另一个把身子缩在大衣里，饶有兴致地听着。

paragraphs.en: At the corner stood a drug store, brilliant with electric lights. When they came into this glare each of them turned simultaneously to gaze upon the other's face.
paragraphs.zh: 街角有家药房，电灯照得通亮。两人走进这片亮光时，同时转过头去看对方的脸。

paragraphs.en: The man from the West stopped suddenly and released his arm.
paragraphs.zh: 从西部来的人突然停住脚步，松开了胳膊。

paragraphs.en: “You're not Jimmy Wells,” he snapped. “Twenty years is a long time, but not long enough to change a man's nose from a Roman to a pug.”
paragraphs.zh: 「你不是吉米·威尔斯，」他厉声说，「二十年是长，可还不至于把一个人的鹰钩鼻变成狮子鼻。」

paragraphs.en: “It sometimes changes a good man into a bad one,” said the tall man. “You've been under arrest for ten minutes, 'Silky' Bob. Chicago thinks you may have dropped over our way and wires us she wants to have a chat with you. Going quietly, are you? That's sensible.”
paragraphs.zh: 「有时候它也能把一个好人变成坏人，」高个子说，「你已经被捕十分钟了，『滑头』鲍勃。芝加哥方面认为你可能跑到我们这儿来了，发电报说要跟你聊聊。乖乖跟我们走，是吧？这才明智。」

paragraphs.en: “Now, before we go to the station here's a note I was asked to hand you. You may read it here at the window. It's from Patrolman Wells.”
paragraphs.zh: 「现在，去警局之前，有人托我交给你一张字条。你就在这窗边看看吧，是巡警威尔斯写的。」

paragraphs.en: The man from the West unfolded the little piece of paper handed him. His hand was steady when he began to read, but it trembled a little by the time he had finished. The note was rather short.
paragraphs.zh: 从西部来的人展开递来的那张小纸片。开始读时他的手还很稳，读到最后却微微发起抖来。字条很短。

paragraphs.en: “Bob: I was at the appointed place on time. When you struck the match to light your cigar I saw it was the face of the man wanted in Chicago. Somehow I couldn't do it myself, so I went around and got a plain clothes man to do the job. JIMMY.”
paragraphs.zh: 「鲍勃：我准时到了约定地点。你划火柴点雪茄的时候，我认出你就是芝加哥通缉的那个人。我实在下不了手，只好绕过去找了个便衣来办这事。吉米。」
